cards.title: Pythagoras and special triangles
cards.body: In a right triangle, $a^2 + b^2 = c^2$, where $c$ is the hypotenuse (opposite the right angle). Common triples: $3, 4, 5$ and $5, 12, 13$ and their multiples. Special triangles: $45^\circ$-$45^\circ$-$90^\circ$ has sides $x, x, x\sqrt{2}$; $30^\circ$-$60^\circ$-$90^\circ$ has sides $x, x\sqrt{3}, 2x$.

cards.title: Worked example: the ladder
cards.problem: A $10$ m ladder leans against a wall with its foot $6$ m from the wall. How high does it reach?

steps.text: The ladder is the hypotenuse: $6^2 + h^2 = 10^2$.
A $6, 8, 10$ triangle is a $3, 4, 5$ triangle doubled.

cards.title: SOH CAH TOA
cards.body: For an acute angle $\theta$ in a right triangle: $\sin\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$, $\cos\theta = \frac{\text{adjacent}}{\text{hypotenuse}}$ and $\tan\theta = \frac{\text{opposite}}{\text{adjacent}}$. The two acute angles add up to $90^\circ$, so $\sin x^\circ = \cos(90 - x)^\circ$.

cards.title: Worked example: a trig ratio
cards.problem: In right triangle $ABC$ the right angle is at $C$, $AC = 5$ and $BC = 12$. Find $\sin A$.

steps.text: For angle $B$, $BC$ is the adjacent side, so $\cos B = \frac{12}{13}$ too: $\sin A = \cos B$ because $A + B = 90^\circ$.

prompts: How do you decide which side is opposite and which is adjacent?
